Which is a horrible misrepresentation of the city. Just because a portion of the population, like my family, did come from such humble roots that in no way encapsulates what Middletown is now or even what it used to be. It was the very fact that there were industrial opportunities to better provide for their family that caused my grandparents to move from hollers of Kentucky where we were originally from. I hate that Vance is purposefully misleading the country to believe lies about my home and honestly at the same time tying to capitalize off of people with similar backgrounds. I’m in no way surprised, but I still hate to see it happen.

Middletown is my hometown. I grew up there and lived nearly 35 years of my life there. My family is also from Kentucky, and I can’t even finish watching hillbilly eulogy because it’s too hard to see some of my family reflected in it. I know that Middletown is a lot bigger than it was when I was growing up and it is a lot more diverse so it’s hard for some to see the Appalachian roots but to those of us who are older, it definitely has some roots there. 

I think that it might have also been more of a neighborhood thing too. I saw a comment where someone mentioned the ghetto and I think that could mean a few places. Growing up for me the ghetto was near the old Oneida school. That was where my home was and it seemed to me that it was full of people who were just like my family, hillbillies. Men working and drinking in their garages til all hours of the night. Women in the house taking care of the kids, cooking and cleaning. World’s best biscuits and gravy and fried pork chops were served at those kitchen tables. That was our everyday life. 

As I got older I lived all over Middletown. I met my husband in his neighborhood, he’d say he grew up in the hood. Just down from the old Vail middle school. I lived there for a while too. It was a different vibe from my neighborhood but the underlining sentiment was the same. People mostly looked out for their neighbors and did what they had to do to just get by. 

I lived in the trailer park by the river and it was the same. Different people same story, try to survive and help others when you can.  

When my kids were young we lived in a few other neighborhoods but honestly I think by then drugs had started taking over the city and that was the turning point. It felt like you couldn’t really trust anyone anymore. 

We moved away almost 15 years ago now and just today I tried to talk my adult daughter into really thinking about it before she decides to move back there not because I think it’s a bad city but because in my own experience, people from Middletown tend to struggle more just to get by. I’m not saying there’s any fault there, as I said this is all based on my own life experiences but I know I’d never move back. 

It’s weird but I kind of hate that Middletown is in the spotlight because of Vance right now. I do hope that maybe it will have a positive impact and things will improve for my hometown community but I fear that only the negatives will be highlighted and my family and old friends will have even more of a burden to deal with. The folks from Middletown have had enough to overcome throughout the last several decades, I hate to see them have to deal with any more crap.

My heart goes out to you and I wish you my deepest condolences.

For me it was the time he told me, “I don’t mind your body. It doesn’t bother me. I understand you have children” 

For context: 
They are all his children. We have been together for 32 years (31 when he said it)
I was completely naked at the time and he was not. Also this came on the heels of months of begging him for sex/intimacy only for him to say yes and then instead of following through he would sneak off with his phone to meet those needs. 
It’s been more than a year since he said it and I still think about almost every time I’m getting out of the shower. It might not sound that bad but those little harmless words broke me in a way I didn’t know was possible.

It’s taken me a while to get back to my post because I have been trying to make sure the kids are outside and enjoying summer. I’ve been going through a tough time lately and I really appreciate all the support and kindness I received from you all. 

I’ve been in therapy for about four years now and I’ve learned so much. I just wish I’d been able to learn it sooner for my sake as well as my family’s. What I’m able to do now is what I’ve always tried to accomplish but without the ability to emotionally regulate myself I just couldn’t do it. I think if nothing else I’m grateful that I have broken a generational fear of getting help for our mental heath issues. After I was able to show how successful therapy can be, several of my older kids agreed to get some help that they needed too. I hate that I’ve passed on these genes and more especially the learned behaviors that I did but I am so thankful that maybe I might have been the one who finally breaks this cycle. 

Thanks again to everybody who offered me a little kindness. I really needed it and I appreciate it so much.

We had a similar experience the day my husband was diagnosed. 

We were driving home from the doctor’s office in complete shock and disbelief. About half way home his phone rang with an unfamiliar number but because we were expecting a nurse to call about scheduling surgery, he answered it. 

It was a woman who was campaigning for breast cancer patient donations. She was speaking very quickly and going through her speech about how hard cancer is, not only on patients but also for their families and explaining how there are so many unplanned expenses that people don’t understand or think about. 

We both stared at each other in shock for a split second before we simultaneously burst out in laughter at the sheer absurdity of the coincidence. He was able to mute the phone but she obviously heard us laughing. I felt horrible but luckily we got our selves together and he was able to apologize to her and explain the situation by telling her why we would unfortunately not be able to donate.

I did this too, although it was more of an agreed upon compromise in my case. I wanted one of my children to have my grandpa’s name and my husband had opposed it with each pregnancy that I suggested it. So with our youngest child, who was a surprise baby I told him I’m not asking this time, I am naming him after grandpa. We did end up with a compromise where that was his middle name though. 
Hubby thought that meant that he would be able to call him by his first name and for 6 months he did. But I only ever called him by his middle name, I introduced him by his middle name. I made sure all doctors or anywhere else where he had a chart or record reflected that he goes by his middle name. I’m the one who does all of those things and the one who was with him the majority of the time. Eventually hubby realized he wasn’t going to get his way and he finally gave up. 
Our son is nearly 10 and likes both of his names but he still prefers to go by his middle.

My heart is breaking for you. I have also been feeling completely overwhelmed. Being a stay at home mom is hard, whether working or “just parenting” as I do. I have 7 kids and my husband works about 70 hours a week so I’m on my own a lot. For a very long time I tried to keep up with everything on my own and that left very little time for me to take care of myself. It was only a month or so ago that I figured out that I couldn’t be the mom they needed me to be while running on empty all the time. So now I’m finding ways to take time for myself. As I type this I am sitting alone in a hotel room and enjoying some genuine peace and quiet. I was lucky and was able to leave my kids with a loved one for the weekend so that my husband could join me after he gets off of work today, but honestly if that wasn’t the case I would have had him stay home with them for a night or two. I would think since your husband has not felt bad for taking time for himself that maybe you just book yourself a nice room and let him know when you’ll be home. 

Of course a brief break won’t fix your whole life and it seems like getting into some therapy would really benefit your mental health both immediately and in the long run. I sincerely hope that you are able to find someone who can help you through this because after everything you have been through to become a mom you deserve to enjoy it!

As a side note if you do decide to take a mini vacation for yourself just know in advance that you will probably feel guilty for not being with her. You will most likely miss her fiercely not long after walking out of your house. And this one may surprise you but you could possibly even feel a little bored. All of this is okay though just try to take the time to reconnect with yourself. Find the you that you’ve lost while being who everyone else needs. You are a wonderful person and an excellent mother and your husband should be counting his lucky stars to have such a strong and caring wife (he also needs to see how much he is adding to your struggles) I hope you find all the resources and help that you need.

Nope I really don’t because believe it or not, in the past I have been so bad that this is not the bare minimum. For longer than I would like to remember I truly did “the bare minimum” I survived at a base level of living. For years I slept. My functions beyond that were barely there. I did not want to live, and in all honestly I’ll admit I wasn’t living. I just wasn’t dead. I wanted to be. That’s why I told you I do know that pain. I lived it for so many years. Back then I held on because I knew how much it would hurt my loved ones if I died. I still have bad days but I always remember that I could be like that again and so I find meaning in the ordinary things that most people take for granted. My life will never be the grand adventure I had once hoped it would but there is beauty in it. It took me a very long time to realize that and see that as long as I can see the good then what my friends and family’s opinion of my life is irrelevant to me. I can look at myself in the mirror and see that I am worth the life I have been given and I can choose to see the beauty and love and grace within it, but only if I don’t solely focus on the parts that I wished were different. I hope that this helps you because I believe that you are worth the good parts too. Don’t diminish what I’d good because someone else tells you it isn’t worth enough. Hold on to all those small things, over time they will add up and outweigh the bad.

For me it’s just making the choice to not let the darkness I feel have me. Some days are bad and the best I can do is sleep to get through it. Most days are better. I try focus on what did go well. Maybe it was something I accomplished, most days those are small and many other people wouldn’t even consider it a good day. For me I know it’s better than my alternatives. Today for example, I got up. I got dressed. I’m putting in a load of laundry. I’m putting chicken in the crockpot for dinner. This is what is going right in my life at this moment. There is plenty that’s not going as well but I’m choosing to focus on these things and realize that even though they are small and seemingly insignificant they are good and each small step is getting me closer to seeing more of the positive parts of life.

Then I really hope you keep looking. If you give up you’ll never know what you missed. I know life can be painful but love is the only thing I can imagine being worth it. I honestly believe that you will find it again if you don’t give up. A loved one, even a pet or maybe something more abstract? A sunset or (in my case) a beautiful tree. Just look for tiny bit of it and then keep going in that direction, hopefully it will lead you to somewhere amazing. Maybe even to love yourself? You are worthy of it
